title: Monitor a host or service with an integration

blocks.content: Nothing sends data to Grafana Cloud yet? An integration fixes that. It sets up a small collector — Grafana Alloy — on your machine and ships prebuilt dashboards, so your first metrics arrive without building anything.
First, find the integration for what you run:
Search for what you want to monitor — a Linux server, Windows, or MySQL, for example — then open its tile from the results.
blocks.tooltip: Type the technology you want to monitor. The results filter as you type.

blocks.content: You found your integration. Everything you need to connect it is on this page.
Now install the collector on the machine you want to monitor:
Click **Run Grafana Alloy**. This opens setup for the collector that gathers and sends your machine's data.
Name a new API token and click **Create token**. The token is how the collector signs in to your stack — create and copy it yourself, this guide never fills in secrets.
The dialog builds an install command that includes your token. Copy it, then run it in a terminal on the machine you're monitoring. When it finishes, Alloy is running.
Back in the dialog, click **Test Alloy connection** to confirm the collector is connected.
Click **Proceed to install integration** to close the dialog.
The collector is running on your machine and sending data to Grafana Cloud.
Click **Install**. This adds the integration's dashboards and alert rules to your stack.
Click **View Dashboards** and open one. Your machine's metrics are already on it.
You're monitoring a real machine on a dashboard you didn't have to build.

One habit worth starting now: your machine produces more metrics than the dashboards use. The **Advanced integration** toggle on the configuration page sends only the subset the dashboards, alerts, and rules need instead of everything — that keeps your bill down as you add more hosts.
